subtitle: Learn essential blues lead techniques including bending, call-and-response, and blues scale application.

introduction.title: The Foundation of Lead Guitar
introduction.text: Blues is the foundation of virtually all modern lead guitar playing. Master blues techniques and you'll have the tools for rock, jazz, country, and beyond. Blues guitar mimics the human voice. Think of your guitar as singing - use bends for vocal inflection, vibrato for warmth, and phrases that "breathe."

columns.title: Blues: The Universal Language
columns.text: Core Elements: String bending, vibrato, call-and-response, chord-tone targeting, blue notes

columns.title: Vocal Approach
columns.text: Practice: Sing a blues melody first, then recreate it on guitar with the same phrasing and expression

cards.title: String Bending
cards.description: The signature sound of blues guitar - bending strings to reach expressive pitches

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Bend the minor 3rd to major 3rd, bend 4th to 5th, add emotional expression

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: B.B. King vibrato bends, Albert King powerful bends

cards.title: Vibrato
cards.description: Rapid pitch variations that add life and emotion to sustained notes

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Add to any sustained note, especially at end of phrases or on chord tones

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: B.B. King butterfly vibrato, Gary Moore wide vibrato

cards.title: Call and Response
cards.description: Musical conversation between vocal-like guitar phrases

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Play a phrase, then "answer" it with a related phrase, like singing

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: B.B. King conversational style, Muddy Waters vocals and guitar

cards.title: Chord-Tone Targeting
cards.description: Landing on chord tones (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th) for harmonic connection

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Outline chord changes, create melodic logic over progression

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: T-Bone Walker chord-based lines, jazz-blues approaches

cards.title: Minor Pentatonic
cards.description: Foundation for all blues playing, works over most chord changes

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A minor pentatonic: A-C-D-E-G

fields.label: Tip
fields.value: Most important scale for blues - master this first

cards.title: Blues Scale
cards.description: Add b5 (blue note) to minor pentatonic for authentic blues sound

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A blues scale: A-C-D-D#-E-G

fields.label: Tip
fields.value: The b5 creates the essential "blue note" tension

cards.title: Major Pentatonic
cards.description: Over major chords, country blues, more upbeat blues styles

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A major pentatonic: A-B-C#-E-F#

fields.label: Tip
fields.value: Great for major blues and country-influenced playing

cards.title: Mixolydian Mode
cards.description: Over dominant 7th chords, blues-rock, Southern rock

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A Mixolydian: A-B-C#-D-E-F#-G

fields.label: Tip
fields.value: Perfect for dominant 7th chord contexts

cards.title: 12-Bar Blues
cards.description: Use A minor pentatonic/blues scale throughout, target chord tones on changes

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: I-I-I-I-IV-IV-I-I-V-IV-I-V

fields.label: Variations
fields.value: Quick change (bar 2), turnaround variations, substitutions

cards.title: 8-Bar Blues
cards.description: Shorter form allows for more concentrated development of ideas

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: I-V-IV-I-I-V-IV-I

fields.label: Variations
fields.value: Common in folk blues, country blues, simpler progressions

cards.title: Minor Blues
cards.description: A minor pentatonic works perfectly, emphasize minor character

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: i-i-i-i-iv-iv-i-i-V-iv-i-V

fields.label: In A
fields.value: Am-Am-Am-Am-Dm-Dm-Am-Am-E7-Dm-Am-E7

fields.label: Variations
fields.value: More melancholic feel, often slower tempos

cards.title: Jazz Blues
cards.description: More complex harmony requires chord-specific scale choices

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: Imaj7-Vi7-IIm7-V7-IVmaj7-VII7-I-V7

fields.label: In A
fields.value: Amaj7-F#7-Bm7-E7-Dmaj7-G7-A-E7

fields.label: Variations
fields.value: Bird blues, bebop blues, sophisticated substitutions

cards.title: King of the Blues Lick
cards.description: B.B. King signature bend from minor 3rd to major 3rd with vibrato

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Bend C to C# over A7 chord, add wide vibrato

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Works over any dominant chord, transpose to different keys

fields.label: Variation
fields.value: Can be done with pre-bend, quarter-tone bends, or slides

cards.title: Albert King Box Move
cards.description: String-skipping lick that moves across multiple strings

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Use aggressive bends and string skipping for power

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Great for climactic moments, building intensity

fields.label: Variation
fields.value: Can be played with hybrid picking or all downstrokes

cards.title: Freddie King Lick
cards.description: Fast triplet run down the minor pentatonic scale

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Alternate picking or economy picking for speed

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Turnarounds, fills between vocal lines

fields.label: Variation
fields.value: Can be played with different rhythmic subdivisions

cards.title: Muddy Waters Slide Lick
cards.description: Slide guitar approach adapted for regular playing

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Use slides between notes instead of individual attacks

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Creates vocal-like phrasing and smooth connections

fields.label: Variation
fields.value: Can be combined with bends for extra expression

cards.title: Quarter-Tone Bends
cards.description: Bend the string slightly (1/4 semitone) for a "crying" or "blue" sound. Common on the minor 3rd. Essential for authentic blues expression.

cards.title: Half-Step Bends
cards.description: Bend up exactly one fret (half-step). Most common bend, especially from minor 3rd to major 3rd. Practice with a tuner to get exact pitch.

cards.title: Whole-Step Bends
cards.description: Bend up two frets (whole step). Requires more finger strength, often used for dramatic effect. Use multiple fingers for support.

cards.title: B.B. King - "The Thrill is Gone"
cards.description: Butterfly vibrato, vocal-like phrasing, minimal notes with maximum expression

fields.label: Learn
fields.value: How to make every note count, call-and-response with vocals

cards.title: Albert King - "Born Under a Bad Sign"
cards.description: Powerful string bending, upside-down guitar technique, aggressive attack

fields.label: Learn
fields.value: How to use bends for emotional impact, string-skipping techniques

cards.title: Freddie King - "Hide Away"
cards.description: Faster blues playing, clean articulation, hybrid picking

fields.label: Learn
fields.value: How to play blues with speed while maintaining clarity

cards.title: Muddy Waters - "Mannish Boy"
cards.description: Slide guitar approach, vocal-guitar conversation, Chicago blues style

fields.label: Learn
fields.value: How guitar can support and enhance vocals, rhythmic blues playing

practiceSection.title: Blues Practice Routine
items: Scale Practice: Practice minor pentatonic and blues scales in all 5 positions. Focus on clean execution.
Bending Practice: Practice quarter, half, and whole-step bends. Use a tuner to ensure accurate pitch.
Lick Learning: Learn classic blues licks and practice them over different chord progressions.
Jamming: Play along with blues backing tracks, focusing on phrasing and expression over speed.
